questions.prompt: What is the difference between try, try?, and try! in Swift? Answer in 2–5 sentences.

rubric.criterion: Explains try is used inside do-catch or throwing functions to catch or pass on errors
Explains try? turns thrown errors into nil, returning an optional
Explains try! disables error propagation and crashes at runtime if an error is thrown

questions.modelAnswer: In Swift, try calls a throwing function inside a do-catch block or another throwing function. The try? keyword turns any thrown error into nil and gives an optional value. The try! keyword disables error propagation and crashes your app at runtime if an error is thrown.

questions.prompt: Why are Swift enums with associated values a good fit for modeling errors, and how do callers inspect them? Answer in 2–5 sentences.

rubric.criterion: Explains that enums group a clear set of related error cases
States that associated values attach extra failure details to specific cases
Mentions that callers can use pattern matching in catch clauses to read those details

questions.modelAnswer: Swift enums work well for errors because they list a clear group of failure cases. Each case can hold associated values with extra details, like a page number or status code. Callers can then use pattern matching in catch clauses to match a case and bind those values.

questions.prompt: Explain when a defer block runs in Swift, including when an error is thrown, and in what order multiple defer blocks execute. Answer in 2–5 sentences.

rubric.criterion: Explains that defer waits until execution leaves the current scope
States that defer runs both on normal exit and when an error is thrown
Explains that multiple defer blocks run in reverse order (last in, first out)

questions.modelAnswer: A defer block runs right before code leaves the current scope. It runs whether the scope ends normally or exits early because an error was thrown. If there are several defer blocks in the same scope, they run in reverse order, with the last one written running first.

sources.title: The Swift Programming Language: Error Handling

questions.prompt: How does Swift error handling differ from exception handling in languages like Java or C++? Answer in 2–5 sentences.

rubric.criterion: Explains that Swift error handling does not unwind the call stack
States that throwing an error has a cost close to returning a normal value
Notes that try marks throwing call sites clearly for compile-time safety

questions.modelAnswer: Unlike Java or C++, Swift error handling does not unwind the call stack. Throwing an error in Swift has a cost close to returning a normal value. The compiler also requires try at every throwing call site, so error paths are clear when you build your code.

questions.prompt: What is the Result type in Swift, and when is it preferred over throwing functions? Answer in 2–5 sentences.

rubric.criterion: Defines Result as an enum with success and failure cases
Explains that Result holds the outcome of an operation as a value
States that it is preferred when storing an outcome for later or passing it to a completion handler

questions.modelAnswer: Result is a standard library enum with .success and .failure cases. It stores the outcome of an operation as a normal value you can pass around or save. Developers prefer Result over throwing functions when saving outcomes for later or passing them to completion handlers.
